Leading our rankings is **Les Misérables** (83/100), a grittier reboot at the refurbished Sondheim Theatre that has won over most critics with its fresh approach to the beloved musical, though purists remain divided. Close behind is **A Soldier's Play** (78/100), Charles Fuller's Pulitzer Prize-winning drama that finally reached Broadway in a stellar revival, proving the work's examination of race and power in the military remains devastatingly relevant decades after it was written.

The season also showcased theatrical risk-taking, from Laura Linney's luminous solo performance in **My Name is Lucy Barton** (71/100)—an intimate adaptation that critics found either mesmerizing or too slight—to Ivo van Hove's polarizing **West Side Story** (68/100), which divided audiences with its radical vision of video design and unconventional staging choices.

With an average critic score of 74/100 across these five productions, the brief 2020 season demonstrated Broadway's ongoing tension between honoring tradition and pushing boundaries. best-broadway-plays-2020.intro:
# Best Broadway Plays Opening in 2020

As we look back from March 2026, the Broadway plays that opened in 2020 represent a fascinating snapshot of theater just before—and in some cases, just after—an unprecedented global disruption. This collection of five productions showcases the range and ambition of American and British theater during a pivotal year.

Leading our rankings is a reimagined **Les Misérables** (83/100), which earns critical acclaim for its grittier approach at the refurbished Sondheim Theatre, though the bold reinterpretation doesn't win over all traditionalists. Close behind, **A Soldier's Play** (78/100) finally brings Charles Fuller's Pulitzer Prize-winning drama to Broadway in a stellar revival that critics agree remains urgently relevant, proving that some stories only grow more essential with time.

The remaining productions reflect Broadway's diversity of vision, from intimate character studies to reimagined classics. Laura Linney commands the stage in **My Name is Lucy Barton** (71/100), a solo adaptation that divides critics between admiration for her luminous performance and questions about the material's theatrical translation. **Grand Horizons** (71/100) offers more traditional boulevard comedy, with Jane Alexander anchoring a familiar but well-executed examination of late-life marriage. Meanwhile, **West Side Story** (68/100) generates the most debate with Ivo van Hove's radical reimagining—a production that critics either embrace for its bold vision or resist for straying too far from beloved source material.

With an average score of 74/100 across these five productions, the class of 2020 demonstrates both Broadway's artistic ambitions and the subjective nature of reinvention. Explore the full reviews to discover which interpretations align with your theatrical sensibilities.

best-broadway-plays-2021.intro:
# Best Broadway Plays That Opened in 2021

As of March 2026, the Broadway shows that debuted in 2021 continue to demonstrate the remarkable artistic resilience and innovation that marked the theater industry's pandemic reopening. This collection of 10 productions, averaging an impressive 81/100 critical score, showcases the diverse range of storytelling that defined this pivotal year—from experimental docudramas to reimagined classics.

Leading the field is **Dana H.**, Lucas Hnath's unconventional docudrama featuring Deirdre O'Connell's extraordinary lip-sync performance to recorded interviews with the playwright's mother. Critics consistently describe the production as mesmerizing and unforgettable, cementing its place as one of the most daring theatrical experiments in recent memory. Close behind, Rebecca Frecknall's **Cabaret at the Kit Kat Club** earns widespread acclaim for its immersive transformation of the August Wilson Theatre (formerly the Playhouse Theatre), proving that classic musicals can still feel urgently contemporary.

The year also saw **The Lehman Trilogy** transfer from the West End, with critics praising Sam Mendes's epic three-hour examination of American capitalism as a theatrical triumph marked by extraordinary ensemble work. Meanwhile, smaller-scale productions like **Is This a Room** and **Lackawanna Blues** demonstrate that intimate storytelling remains just as powerful as grand spectacle.

From Marianne Elliott's gender-swapped **Company** to Antoinette Chinonye Nwandu's **Pass Over**—which made history as the first show to reopen Broadway after the shutdown—these productions collectively represent a snapshot of theater at a transformative moment. Whether you're drawn to experimental formats, immersive revivals, or powerful solo performances, this guide highlights the essential shows from Broadway's historic return.

best-broadway-plays-2022.intro:
# Best Broadway Plays That Opened in 2022

As of March 2026, the Broadway shows that premiered in 2022 continue to demonstrate the remarkable artistic vitality of that season. With an average critic score of 83/100 across these ten productions, the year stands out for its concentration of Pulitzer Prize-winning works and innovative storytelling.

**Kimberly Akimbo** leads the field with an 88/100 score, earning widespread critical acclaim for its distinctive blend of comedy and emotional depth. The musical's quirky sensibility and heartfelt approach have resonated strongly with reviewers. Close behind, both **Into the Woods** and **A Strange Loop** tie at 86/100, representing vastly different theatrical experiences—the former a stripped-down Sondheim revival that serves as a fitting tribute to the late composer, and the latter Michael R. Jackson's brazenly original meta-musical that critics praise for its brutal honesty.

The 2022 season proved particularly notable for bringing Pulitzer Prize-winning plays to Broadway stages. Works like Suzan-Lori Parks' **Topdog/Underdog**, Stephen Adly Guirgis's **Between Riverside and Crazy**, Paula Vogel's **How I Learned to Drive**, and Martyna Majok's **Cost of Living** all found new life in revival or premiere productions. Tom Stoppard's **Leopoldstadt**, while not a Pulitzer winner, stands as the playwright's deeply personal reckoning with Holocaust history.

The range spans from Mike Birbiglia's solo storytelling to Jordan E. Cooper's provocative satire **Ain't No Mo'**, showcasing the breadth of theatrical voices that defined the season. For theatergoers exploring Broadway's recent history, these productions represent some of the most critically celebrated work of the early 2020s.

best-broadway-plays-2023.intro:
# Best Broadway Plays That Opened in 2023

As we look back from March 2026, the Broadway plays that premiered in 2023 represent one of the strongest theatrical seasons in recent memory, with an average critic score of 82/100 across our featured productions.

The season's crown jewel is **Merrily We Roll Along**, Maria Friedman's revelatory revival that finally unlocks the potential of Sondheim's infamous 1981 flop. With 31 reviews averaging 85/100, critics celebrate its emotionally resonant performances and the production's ability to illuminate what audiences missed four decades ago. Equally impressive is **Stranger Things: The First Shadow**, which defies expectations by transcending its source material—the West End import earns the same 85/100 score through technically stunning stagecraft that works as breathtaking theatre regardless of familiarity with the Netflix series.

**Appropriate** follows closely behind at 83/100, with Sarah Paulson anchoring Branden Jacobs-Jenkins's searing family drama that critics consider a modern masterpiece. The season also brought important revivals like **Purlie Victorious** (82/100), Ossie Davis's 1961 satire finding bracingly relevant new life, and **Parade** (82/100), whose urgent themes resonated powerfully with contemporary audiences through Ben Platt and Micaela Diamond's performances.

The breadth of this lineup—from Alex Edelman's solo show **Just for Us** to the Pulitzer-winning **Fat Ham**, from the Cuban rhythms of **Buena Vista Social Club** to the immersive rock drama **Stereophonic**—demonstrates 2023's remarkable range. Whether you're catching final performances or discovering these productions through cast recordings and future productions, these plays represent essential contemporary American theatre.

best-broadway-plays-2024.intro:
# Best Broadway Plays

As Broadway enters March 2026, the shows that premiered in 2024 continue to demonstrate exceptional staying power, with an impressive average critic score of 83/100 across our top ten selections.

Leading the pack is **Stereophonic**, David Adjmi's meticulously crafted drama about a 1970s rock band in the studio. With a score of 88/100 from 22 reviews, critics consistently praise its authentic portrayal of the creative process and its ability to capture the tension and artistry of making music. Equally acclaimed is **Operation Mincemeat**, the grassroots British sensation that earned its Broadway transfer through sheer word-of-mouth momentum, with critics celebrating its inventive energy and tight ensemble work.

The 2024 season proves particularly strong for innovative storytelling. **Maybe Happy Ending** brings a robot love story to the musical stage with surprising emotional depth, while Cole Escola's **Oh, Mary!** reimagines Mary Todd Lincoln as a cabaret-obsessed narcissist in what critics describe as a comedic tour de force. These productions sit alongside prestigious revivals like George C. Wolfe's **Gypsy**, featuring Audra McDonald's deeply personal interpretation of Mama Rose, and a lavish new staging of **Oliver!** that balances Dickensian darkness with Lionel Bart's beloved score.

Rounding out the list are intimate dramas like **Mary Jane**, Amy Herzog's understated portrait of maternal devotion, and bold experimental works such as **Illinoise**, Justin Peck's dance-musical adaptation of Sufjan Stevens' album. **Suffs** brings the suffrage movement to vibrant musical life through Shaina Taub's tuneful score.

Whether you're drawn to sweeping revivals, innovative new musicals, or intimate dramas, the class of 2024 offers compelling options across every theatrical taste.

best-broadway-plays-2025.intro:
# Best Broadway Plays

As March 2026 arrives, Broadway audiences continue to enjoy a rich selection of plays that opened throughout 2025, ranging from bold new works to carefully reimagined classics. This month's top ten plays demonstrate the breadth of theatrical storytelling currently on offer, with an impressive average critic score of 84/100.

Leading the field is Ivo van Hove's minimalist revival of **All My Sons**, which earns widespread acclaim for its emotional intensity and exceptional ensemble work. Arthur Miller's classic family drama proves as resonant as ever in van Hove's stripped-down staging. Close behind, **The 25th Annual Putnam County Spelling Bee** celebrates its 20th anniversary with a revival that critics describe as joyous and tender, with the musical's airtight writing and emotional depth earning fresh appreciation from reviewers.

Family-friendly fare also makes a strong showing with **Paddington The Musical**, which enchants critics through its remarkably lifelike bear puppet—described as a genuine theatrical marvel. Meanwhile, new American plays command attention: Sanaz Toossi's Pulitzer-winning **English** receives strong praise for its sensitive exploration of language and identity, while Branden Jacobs-Jenkins delivers another characteristically sharp family drama with **Purpose**.

The season also features ambitious works like Jen Silverman's **Liberation**, a feminist memory play praised for its timeliness and superb performances, and the darkly comic musical **Dead Outlaw**, which tells the bizarre true story of outlaw Elmer McCurdy's afterlife. A revival of **Ragtime** rounds out the highlights, with Joshua Henry's powerhouse performance drawing particular acclaim.

best-broadway-plays-2026.intro:
# Best Broadway Plays of 2026

March 2026 brings a notably lean opening schedule for new Broadway plays, with just one production making its debut this month. While the limited roster reflects the challenging economics facing straight plays on Broadway, the sole entry demonstrates the enduring appeal of well-crafted psychological drama.

**Bug** stands as the month's singular offering, marking the long-awaited Broadway premiere of Tracy Letts' 1996 psychological thriller. With a solid critic score of 74/100 across 35 reviews, the production earns mostly positive notices for its intense exploration of paranoia and delusion. Originally produced by Chicago's Red Orchid Theatre three decades ago, the play arrives on Broadway with renewed relevance, its themes of conspiracy and fractured reality resonating in contemporary discourse. Critics particularly praise the production's claustrophobic staging and committed performances, though some note the material's deliberately unsettling nature may not appeal to all theatergoers.

The sparse March schedule underscores a broader trend in commercial theater, where plays increasingly struggle to secure Broadway berths amid rising production costs and risk-averse producers. That **Bug** makes it to the Great White Way at all speaks to both the strength of Letts' reputation—bolstered by his Pulitzer Prize-winning **August: Osage County**—and the theater community's ongoing commitment to provocative, challenging work.

For audiences seeking substantive dramatic fare this month, **Bug** offers a compelling if confronting option that showcases the raw power of theatrical storytelling. Those planning their spring theater calendar should consider catching this production while monitoring announcements for upcoming play openings in the months ahead.
